claims.claim: Claude Opus 5 (API ID claude-opus-5) has a 1M token context window, 128K max output on the synchronous Messages API, and up to 300K output tokens on the Message Batches API with the output-300k-2026-03-24 beta header. Default effort is high and thinking is adaptive. Legacy status; retirement not sooner than July 24, 2027.

Start with the default effort (high) on Claude Opus 5 and tune from evals: use low and medium liberally as the primary control for token cost and latency where quality holds, step up to xhigh for demanding coding and agentic work, and max only when unconstrained token spending is justified. All five effort levels are supported. Re-run an effort sweep rather than reusing effort settings carried over from an earlier model.

On Claude Opus 5, thinking runs by default (adaptive) and can be disabled only at effort high or below. A request with thinking {type: disabled} at xhigh or max effort returns a 400 error. Sending thinking {type: enabled, budget_tokens} or {type: between_tools} also returns a 400 error. Prefer keeping thinking on at lower effort over disabling it.

When running Claude Opus 5 at xhigh or max effort, set a large max_tokens so the model has room to think and act across subagents and tool calls; starting at 64k tokens and tuning from there is a reasonable default.

Effort on Claude Opus 5 controls thinking volume, not visible response length. Its default user-facing responses are longer than prior Opus models, so control length with an explicit conciseness instruction in the prompt (optionally repeated as a short reminder near the end of a long system prompt) rather than by lowering effort.

Claude Opus 5 verifies and self-corrects without being told. Remove explicit verification or re-check instructions (for example 'include a final verification step', 'use a subagent to verify', 'double-check your answer') and legacy harness verification steps, because they cause over-verification and wasted tokens with no loss in quality when removed.

Claude Opus 5 delegates to subagents more readily than prior models. Give explicit guidance on when delegation is warranted (large, independent, parallelizable work; not small tasks; not verification of its own work) or set deterministic caps, such as the CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH and CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS environment variables and the Agent SDK max_budget_usd option.

For code review prompts on Claude Opus 5, avoid filters like 'only report high-severity issues' or 'be conservative', since the model may follow them literally and report less. Ask it to report everything and filter in a separate pass.

With thinking disabled, Claude Opus 5 can occasionally write tool calls as text instead of a structured tool_use block, or emit internal XML tags such as thinking tags in visible output. Mitigate by keeping thinking enabled at lower effort; if it must stay off, remove any 'do not think' rule and use a general instruction: say a brief sentence before a tool call, say so if no tool fits instead of guessing, and do not include internal or system XML tags. Do not name specific tags.

Prompts, skills, and tool descriptions that ask Claude Opus 5 to write out its thinking or reasoning verbatim or in a fixed format may be declined with the reasoning_extraction refusal category. Ask for a short explanation of the answer or a summary of actions taken instead, or keep thinking on and read the summarized thinking blocks (display: summarized).

Claude Opus 5 narrates readily during agentic work and can expand task scope. Tune narration by describing the desired cadence and giving positive examples; constrain scope on narrow tasks with an explicit scope instruction; and add explicit length calibration for Claude-authored documents, which tend to run longer than on prior models.
Callers that used the none or minimal reasoning effort should start with low and compare results; GPT-6 Astra does not support the none reasoning effort.

claims.claim: Effort is the primary control for intelligence, latency, and cost on Claude Fable 5.1. The default is high. Start at high, then test low, medium, xhigh, and max against your own evals, and re-run the sweep even if you already ran one on Claude Fable 5, because effort level names do not map to the same amount of thinking across models.

Thinking on claude-fable-5-1 is adaptive and always on, steered by effort. Manual extended thinking (thinking.type enabled with budget_tokens) is not accepted on later models. Context window is 1M tokens and max output is 128K tokens on the synchronous Messages API.

Forced tool choice is not supported on claude-fable-5-1. tool_choice of type any or type tool returns a 400 invalid_request_error on the Messages API, Message Batches API, and token counting endpoint. Use auto or none, and steer tool use through prompting or tool descriptions instead.

Fable 5.1 writes fewer user-facing progress updates during long tool-calling turns. Progress notes arrive as thinking blocks that are empty under the default thinking.display of omitted, so set display to updates (beta header thinking-display-updates-2026-08-18) or summarized to receive them. Remove system prompt lines that suppress narration, such as holding all findings for the final response, and add a short line saying when updates are wanted if still needed.

In coding and computer-use agent loops where independent next calls are only implied, Fable 5.1 may issue one tool call per turn. Mitigate by appending the one-sentence instruction 'First privately list what you need next; then request every item that doesn't depend on another's result in this one response.' after each set of tool results, as a turn-scoped system message (role system, clear_at next_user_message, beta header mid-conversation-system-clear-at-2026-08-21) or, without the beta, as a text block after the tool_result blocks.

Keep conversation history append-only on Fable 5.1: append each assistant turn exactly as returned with thinking blocks included, and do not edit earlier turns, the system prompt, or the tool list between requests. A thinking block is valid only while everything before it is unchanged, and edits also restart the prompt cache. Only Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 can read Fable 5.1's thinking blocks. Cache reads cost $0.25 per MTok.

Fable 5.1 uses bold, headers, lists, and quotation marks less than earlier models, so remove anti-formatting language from prompts or replace it with a rule stating when formatting is appropriate (lists when asked or when content is multifaceted, minimal formatting when requested, plain prose for conversational or emotional exchanges).

Fable 5.1 is more likely than Fable 5 to rewrite an entire text file instead of making a targeted edit. Append to the system prompt or first user message: 'The number of tokens used to edit files is best minimized, all else being equal. Therefore, when it will not affect the end result, try to surgically edit a file rather than rewrite the entire thing.'

At xhigh and max effort, Fable 5.1 can draft a long deliverable in its thinking and then write it again as the reply. Prefer high for such requests. If using xhigh or max, set max_tokens to cover thinking plus reply, and append a note to the user message stating that reasoning and reply share one limit of about [max_tokens] tokens and that the full deliverable should not be composed in reasoning and then again as the reply.

At low effort Fable 5.1 calls search and retrieval tools less often and answers from memory more. Raise effort for those turns, or add a system prompt nudge saying that names not confidently recognized, or from fast-moving areas, must be searched as the user wrote them even when background knowledge exists.

Prompts, skills, and tool descriptions that ask Fable 5.1 to write out its thinking or reasoning may be declined with the reasoning_extraction category (stop_reason refusal). Ask for a short explanation or a summary of actions taken instead, or read reasoning from summarized thinking blocks (display summarized).

For long autonomous work, Fable 5.1 sometimes ends a turn by describing next steps or asking permission for work already requested. Mitigate with a system prompt block that says the user is not watching and cannot answer mid-task, tells the model to proceed on reversible actions that follow from the request and stop only for destructive actions or genuine scope changes, and says to do the work now if the last paragraph is a plan or promise. Treat the request or approved plan as the scope of the deliverable.

Claude Sonnet 5 (API id claude-sonnet-5, legacy, released June 30, 2026) has a 1M token context window, 128K max output on the synchronous Messages API, and up to 300K output tokens on the Message Batches API with the output-300k-2026-03-24 beta header. Text and images in, text out.
Setting temperature, top_p, or top_k on Claude Sonnet 5 returns a 400 error. Omit these parameters and steer tone and variety through system-prompt instructions instead.
Manual extended thinking (thinking: {type: "enabled", budget_tokens: N}) is not supported on Claude Sonnet 5 and returns a 400 error. Use adaptive thinking with the effort parameter instead.

On Claude Sonnet 5 adaptive thinking is on by default: a request with no thinking field runs with adaptive thinking (on Sonnet 4.6 the same request ran without thinking). To turn thinking off entirely, pass thinking: {type: "disabled"}. Revisit max_tokens for workloads that previously ran without thinking, because max_tokens caps thinking plus response text.

The effort parameter on Claude Sonnet 5 defaults to high. For the hardest coding and agentic tasks raise it to xhigh; max has no token-spend constraints; medium suits cost-sensitive work; low is for short, scoped, latency-sensitive tasks. Effort levels are respected strictly, especially low, so at low and medium the model scopes work to what was asked and may under-think moderately complex tasks. If reasoning is shallow, raise effort rather than prompting around it.

Claude Sonnet 5 uses a new tokenizer that produces roughly 30 percent more tokens for the same text than Sonnet 4.6, so max_tokens limits tuned for Sonnet 4.6 may truncate equivalent output. At high, xhigh, or max effort leave max_tokens headroom for thinking and tool calls, or the response can be mostly thinking followed by a truncated answer with stop_reason max_tokens; raising max_tokens or dropping to medium effort resolves it.

Claude Sonnet 5 is more agentic than Sonnet 4.6 and uses tools more readily, but with thinking disabled it is less likely to reach for tools. If you rely on tool calls with thinking off, add an explicit nudge in the system prompt. High or xhigh effort increases tool usage in agentic search and coding, and prompts should say when and how to use each tool.

Claude Sonnet 5 follows instructions literally, especially at lower effort: it does not generalize an instruction from one item to another or infer unstated requests. State the scope explicitly when an instruction should apply broadly (for example, apply this formatting to every section, not just the first).

For code-review harnesses, Claude Sonnet 5 follows severity or confidence filters in the prompt (such as only report high-severity issues) more faithfully than earlier models, which can lower measured recall. Ask it to report every issue with a confidence level and estimated severity and do filtering in a separate stage, or give a concrete reporting threshold instead of qualitative words like important.

Claude Sonnet 5 calibrates response length to task complexity. To reduce verbosity add an instruction such as concise, focused responses with minimal examples; positive examples of the desired concision work better than negative instructions. Remove scaffolding that forces interim progress messages, since the model already gives regular progress updates in long agentic traces.
Claude Sonnet 5 is a legacy model (status Active, retirement not sooner than June 30, 2027); the docs advise considering migration to Claude Sonnet 5.5 (claude-sonnet-5-5).

claims.claim: Claude API model ID is claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 (pinned snapshot); claude-haiku-4-5 is a convenience alias that resolves to it. Context window is 200K tokens and max output is 64K tokens (synchronous Messages API). Haiku 4.5 is labeled Legacy; Claude Haiku 5.5 is the current Haiku model.
Haiku 4.5 uses manual extended thinking (thinking: {type: "enabled", budget_tokens: N}), not adaptive thinking; the effort parameter is not supported on it (default effort listed as 'Not supported').

For Haiku 4.5 extended thinking, budget_tokens must be at least 1,024 and less than max_tokens (thinking tokens count toward max_tokens). Start near 1,024 for simple tasks and 16,000+ for complex tasks; for budgets above 32k use batch processing. Changing budget_tokens between requests invalidates message-level prompt cache breakpoints, so hold the budget stable across a cached conversation.

Sending thinking: {type: "adaptive"} to Haiku 4.5 returns a 400 error; keep budget_tokens on this model. Haiku 4.5 does not support interleaved thinking (the interleaved-thinking-2025-05-14 beta header is accepted but ignored on the Claude API), and the API strips previous turns' thinking blocks from history when they are passed back.

Haiku 4.5 pricing is $1 per MTok input and $5 per MTok output; 5m cache write $1.25/MTok, 1h cache write $2/MTok, cache read $0.10/MTok; Batch API gives a 50% discount. Reliable knowledge cutoff is Feb 2025 and training data cutoff is Jul 2025.

claims.claim: Thinking counts toward max_tokens even when thinking content is not returned, so size max_tokens for thinking plus the reply; for agentic coding set max_tokens to 128,000, the model maximum, and stream the response.

claims.claim: On agentic coding at low and medium effort the model sometimes checks in before the work is done: it may pause to confirm a plan, ask a question it could answer itself, or stop after one part of a multipart task. claims.claim: Adaptive thinking is always on for claude-opus-5-5. Send no thinking field or thinking {type: adaptive}. thinking {type: disabled} and thinking {type: enabled, budget_tokens: N} are rejected with a 400 invalid_request_error.

Control thinking depth only through output_config.effort. All five levels (low, medium, high, xhigh, max) are supported. The default is medium (Claude Opus 5 defaulted to high), so set effort explicitly and re-run an effort sweep on your own evals rather than carrying over an Opus 5 setting.

max_tokens is a hard limit on thinking plus response text. At a given effort level Opus 5.5 tends to think more per turn than Opus 5, especially at xhigh and max. Set max_tokens high; start at 64k when running xhigh or max, and 128,000 (the model maximum) has worked well for long agentic coding turns.

Forced tool use is rejected with a 400 error: tool_choice {type: any} and {type: tool, name: ...} are not supported. Use tool_choice auto (default) or none; for schema-valid JSON use strict: true strict tool use or structured outputs, and state in the prompt when a tool applies.

Omit temperature, top_p and top_k, and do not end messages with a prefilled assistant turn (it is rejected). Use prompting, structured outputs, or system prompt instructions to shape behavior instead.

Responses can begin with thinking blocks, so read content by block type rather than position (not content[0].text). In tool-use loops, return thinking blocks complete and unmodified (including empty ones); edited, reordered or dropped thinking blocks cause a 400 error. thinking.display defaults to omitted (empty thinking field); set display summarized to get readable summaries.

Text the model writes between tool calls comes back as progress-update thinking blocks, empty at the default display, so a client rendering only text blocks goes quiet. Set thinking.display to updates (beta, header thinking-display-updates-2026-08-18) or summarized to receive them.

Changing the top-level effort value between requests invalidates the prompt cache. To change effort mid-conversation while keeping the cache, use the per-message effort change (beta). Keep the conversation append-only: editing the system prompt, tools or earlier turns invalidates earlier thinking blocks, so use mid-conversation system messages instead.

If an Opus 5 integration ran with thinking disabled, start at low effort and measure (move to medium if quality drops), remove instructions asking the model to write its reasoning into the response, and read reasoning from summarized thinking blocks. Prompts pushing reasoning into response text may be declined with the reasoning_extraction refusal category.

For unattended agent loops, a text-only end_turn can be a progress report rather than completion. Keep a task checklist, send a follow-up user message naming open items, cap automatic continuations at two or three, and optionally add a system prompt paragraph naming the early-stop patterns to avoid (set from the first request of the session to keep the cache and thinking blocks valid).

Computer use must be declared with the computer_toolset_20260801 toolset with no beta header; computer_20251124 returns a 400 on the Claude API (it still works on Amazon Bedrock with the computer-use-2025-11-24 beta header).

claude-opus-5-5 has a 1M-token context window with no context-window beta header needed, 128K max output (300K on the Message Batches API with the output-300k-2026-03-24 beta header), a 512-token minimum cacheable prompt, and fast mode via speed: fast on the Claude API with no beta header. Pricing is $4 input / $20 output per MTok.

reasoning.effort accepts none, low, medium, high, xhigh for gpt-5.2; none is the default. If more thinking is needed, increase slowly to medium and test. With none, prompt the model to outline its steps before answering.

temperature, top_p and logprobs are only supported with gpt-5.2 when reasoning effort is none; sending them with any other effort setting errors. Use reasoning effort, verbosity and max_output_tokens to steer instead.

Use the Responses API with gpt-5.2 so the previous turn's chain of thought is passed between turns (fewer reasoning tokens, higher cache hit rates, lower latency); passing CoT exists only in Responses, not Chat Completions. gpt-5.2 is served on Chat Completions, Responses and Batch.

The verbosity parameter (low, medium, high) is retained for gpt-5.2 and defaults to medium; low reduces output tokens and latency, and verbosity can still be steered in the prompt after setting it to low.

Migrate to gpt-5.2 by switching the model without changing the prompt, pinning reasoning_effort to match the prior model (GPT-4o/4.1 start at none; GPT-5 keeps its value except minimal becomes none; GPT-5.1 keeps its value), running evals, and tuning prompts only if results regress, one change at a time.

gpt-5.2 is more concise and plan-forward than GPT-5.1 and needs the preferred output length stated in the prompt, for example 3-6 sentences or at most 5 bullets for typical answers, and two sentences or fewer for yes/no questions.

gpt-5.2 may produce more code or UI than the minimal spec requires; constrain scope explicitly (for example 'implement EXACTLY and ONLY what the user requests', no extra features or invented styling).
For gpt-5.2 inputs over about 10k tokens, have the model build a short outline of relevant sections and restate key constraints before answering, anchoring claims to specific sections.

gpt-5.2 takes more tool actions in interactive flows than GPT-5.1; prompting can reduce this. Parallelize independent reads, and a system/developer instruction can require a short explanation before each tool call (preambles). tool_choice with allowed_tools restricts the model to a subset of tools.

For long, tool-heavy gpt-5.2 workflows, use POST /v1/responses/compact after major milestones rather than every turn, treat returned items as opaque, and keep prompts functionally identical when resuming.

gpt-5.2 specs: 400,000-token context window, 128,000 max output tokens, text and image input with text-only output, snapshot gpt-5.2-2025-12-11, knowledge cutoff Aug 31, 2025; supports function calling, structured outputs, web search, file search, prompt caching, apply_patch and MCP tools in Responses. The page lists it as a previous flagship, and the deprecations page lists gpt-5.2-chat-latest (not gpt-5.2) for shutdown on Aug 10, 2026.
Call gpt-5.3-codex through the Responses API (v1/responses). The model page lists Chat Completions, Assistants, Batch, Realtime, Fine-tuning and Embeddings as not supported.
gpt-5.3-codex accepts reasoning effort values low, medium, high and xhigh.
Use medium reasoning effort as the all-around default for interactive coding with gpt-5.3-codex. Reserve high or xhigh for the hardest tasks.

When using gpt-5.3-codex, store each assistant output item with its phase value (null, commentary or final_answer) and send it back in later requests. phase is supported only on assistant items, so do not add it to user messages. The guide says correct implementation is required, and dropping it causes significant performance degradation.

For preambles, prompt gpt-5.3-codex to give a 1-sentence acknowledgment and a 1-2 sentence plan before any tool calls. Keep most updates to 1-2 sentences, aim for an update every 1-3 execution steps, and never go more than 6 steps or 10 tool calls without one. Mid-rollout updates are promptable for this model, unlike earlier Codex models.

gpt-5.3-codex supports function calling, hosted shell, skills and web search as Responses API tools. It also supports streaming, structured outputs, image input and prompt caching, with a 400k context window, 272k max input and 128k max output.
Prompt caching is supported for gpt-5.3-codex, and cached input is billed at $0.175 per 1M tokens against $1.75 for uncached input.
gpt-5.4 reasoning effort accepts none, low, medium, high, xhigh, and the default is none, so set reasoning effort explicitly when reasoning is needed.

Treat reasoning effort as a last-mile tuning knob: use none for execution-heavy work, medium or higher for research-heavy work, raise slowly from none to medium, and avoid xhigh as a default unless evals show clear benefit.

Before raising reasoning effort on gpt-5.4, first add completeness_contract, verification_loop and tool_persistence_rules blocks (sections wrapped in tags of those names) to the prompt; at effort none, ask the model to outline its steps before answering.

temperature, top_p, and logprobs are supported on gpt-5.4 only when reasoning effort is none; requests including them at any other effort fail. Use reasoning effort, verbosity, and max_output_tokens instead.

gpt-5.4 works best with the Responses API, which preserves prior reasoning between turns (fewer reasoning tokens, higher cache hit rates, lower latency); passing chain of thought exists only in Responses, and previous_response_id is the simplest multi-turn path. Responses uses nested reasoning.effort and text.verbosity; Chat Completions uses top-level reasoning_effort and verbosity.

gpt-5.4 verbosity is configurable as low, medium, or high and defaults to medium; lower verbosity cuts output tokens and latency, and for code, low yields shorter code with minimal commentary while medium/high yield longer, more structured code.

With gpt-5.4 in the Responses API, round-trip the phase parameter (commentary vs final_answer) on assistant messages when replaying history, never add phase to user messages; dropping it can cause preambles to be treated as final answers.

For gpt-5.4 tool use: restrict callable tools via allowed tools in tool_choice (mode auto or required) while listing the full toolkit in tools to improve prompt caching; use tool search to defer tool loading; enable preambles with an instruction like 'Before you call a tool, explain why you are calling it.'

gpt-5.4 migration: it is meant as a drop-in replacement for gpt-5.2 with default settings; switch the model first, pin reasoning_effort, run evals, then change one thing at a time. Start with the smallest prompt that passes evals and add prompt blocks only for measured failures.

gpt-5.4 has a 1,050,000-token context window and 128,000 max output tokens, supports Chat Completions, Responses, and Batch, and prompts over 272K input tokens are billed at 2x input and 1.5x output; pin the snapshot gpt-5.4-2026-03-05 for consistent behavior.
gpt-5.4-mini supports reasoning.effort values none (default), low, medium, high and xhigh. Because the default is none, set reasoning.effort explicitly whenever you need reasoning.

gpt-5.4-mini is supported on Chat Completions, Responses and Batch endpoints. Tools (function calling, web search, file search, tool search, code interpreter, hosted shell, apply patch, skills, computer use, MCP) are listed under the Responses API. Realtime, Assistants, fine-tuning and embeddings are not supported.

gpt-5.4-mini has a 400,000-token context window, max 272,000 input tokens and max 128,000 output tokens. It takes text and image input and produces text output only. The only listed snapshot is gpt-5.4-mini-2026-03-17. Prompt caching and structured outputs are supported.

For gpt-5.4-mini, prompt for literal behavior. It is more literal, makes fewer assumptions and may ask follow-up questions unless told otherwise. Put critical rules first, specify the exact step order, separate 'do the action' from 'report the action', and define ambiguity behavior (ask, abstain or proceed) and packaging rules.
For gpt-5.4-mini, use scoped output-stop wording such as 'after the final JSON, output nothing further' rather than 'output nothing else'.
For smaller GPT-5.4 models, structure prompts in this order: task, critical rule, exact step order, edge cases or clarification behavior, output format, one correct example.

On the GPT-5.4 family, temperature, top_p and logprobs work only with reasoning effort none and other settings return an error. For similar control use reasoning.effort, text.verbosity or max_output_tokens. The page states this for GPT-5.4 and does not restate it for the mini model.

When migrating o4-mini or gpt-4.1-mini workloads, the documented starting point is gpt-5.4-mini. Treat reasoning effort as a last-mile tuning knob. Before raising effort, add completeness_contract, verification_loop and tool_persistence_rules prompt blocks, and avoid xhigh unless evals show a clear benefit.

For GPT-5.4, text.verbosity (low, medium, high) is configurable and defaults to medium. For long-running Responses agents that replay assistant history manually, preserve each original phase value (commentary or final_answer), and do not add phase to user messages. The page states this for GPT-5.4 and does not restate it for the mini model.

When calling reasoning models with function calling, use the Responses API and pass back the reasoning items returned with the last function call along with the function output, for example via previous_response_id. Reasoning tokens count against max_output_tokens and are billed as output tokens. Reserve at least 25,000 tokens for reasoning and output when starting out.
GPT-5.5 reasoning.effort supports none, low, medium (default), high and xhigh.

Use xhigh reasoning effort only for the hardest asynchronous agentic tasks; reserve none for latency-critical work without multi-step tool use, and for latency-sensitive workflows that still need tool use or planning test low before none. Raise effort only when evals show a measurable quality gain.

Treat GPT-5.5 as a new model family to tune for, not a drop-in replacement: start from a fresh, minimal prompt, write outcome-first prompts with success criteria and stopping conditions, and cut step-by-step process guidance unless the path matters.

text.verbosity defaults to medium for GPT-5.5; setting it to low gives more concise output than low did on GPT-5.4. Control answer length separately from reasoning quality using word budgets, section counts, or JSON-only output.

Use the Responses API for reasoning, tool-calling and multi-turn use with GPT-5.5; use previous_response_id for multi-turn state, or for stateless/Zero Data Retention flows pass back the returned output items each turn. When replaying assistant items manually keep each phase value unchanged (commentary for intermediate updates, final_answer for the completed answer) and never add phase to user messages.

Avoid absolute language such as ALWAYS and NEVER for judgment calls in GPT-5.5 prompts (reserve it for true invariants); remove output schema definitions from the prompt and use Structured Outputs instead; do not add the current date since the model knows the current UTC date.

For GPT-5.5 tool use, put most tool-specific guidance in the tool descriptions rather than the system prompt, prefer OpenAI-hosted tools where they fit, and use tool search to load only relevant definitions for large tool catalogs.
For multi-step or tool-heavy GPT-5.5 tasks, ask for a brief user-visible preamble of one or two sentences before tool calls that states the first step, which improves time to first visible token.

For GPT-5.5 prompt caching, put stable content first and dynamic user-specific content last, set a stable prompt_cache_key for requests sharing a prefix (spreading busy groups across multiple keys), and track usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens to measure reuse.

gpt-5.5 has a 1,050,000-token context window and 128,000 max output tokens, is served on Chat Completions, Responses and Batch endpoints (not Realtime or Assistants), and prompts over 272K input tokens are billed at 2x input and 1.5x output for the full session.
Opus 4.6 does not think unless you ask it to. To get thinking, explicitly send thinking: {type: "adaptive"} rather than relying on the default.
Do not cap thinking with budget_tokens on Opus 4.6, because that setting is deprecated there. Use adaptive thinking, control depth with effort, and use max_tokens as the hard ceiling.

Opus 4.6 explores a lot up front, so remove or weaken prompts that push for thoroughness. Replace blanket defaults such as 'Default to using [tool]' with targeted wording such as 'Use [tool] when it would enhance your understanding'. If it still over-explores, lower effort.

When Opus 4.6 thinks too much, add explicit instructions that limit its reasoning (for example, choose an approach, commit to it, and revisit only on contradicting new information), or lower the effort setting.

Drop aggressive tool and skill triggering language written for older models, such as 'CRITICAL: You MUST use this tool when...'. Use plain wording such as 'Use this tool when...', because Opus 4.6 follows the system prompt closely and will overtrigger.
Do not prefill the final assistant turn for Opus 4.6. Prefill returns a 400 error on this model, so get the format you want from instructions or structured outputs instead.

In agentic deployments, add a reversibility and confirmation rule to the prompt. The rule should tell Opus 4.6 to ask before destructive, hard-to-reverse or externally visible actions, such as deleting files, force-pushing or posting to external services.
Limit subagent use in the prompt. Opus 4.6 tends to spawn subagents when a direct call such as grep would be faster and enough, so say when delegating is warranted.

Add explicit minimal-scope guidance for coding work: only make changes that are requested or clearly necessary, with no extra files, abstractions or configurability. Opus 4.6 tends to over-engineer without it.

To reduce how often an adaptive-thinking model thinks, lower the effort level first. Use system-prompt or per-message steering phrases only if thinking still triggers wrongly, and measure quality before shipping.

Use the exact model ID claude-sonnet-4-6 on the Claude API (Bedrock InvokeModel uses anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6). Context window is 1M tokens, max synchronous output is 128K tokens (up to 300K on the Message Batches API with the output-300k-2026-03-24 beta header). claims.claim: Use the effort parameter as the main control for how much Claude Haiku 5.5 thinks (it replaces budget_tokens). Default is medium; use low for chat, short tool tasks and high-volume simple requests; high for knowledge work, longer agent tasks and strict instruction following; xhigh and max only when evals justify the cost.

Send thinking as {"type":"adaptive"} (or omit it) with output_config.effort; thinking {"type":"enabled","budget_tokens":N} returns a 400 error. thinking {"type":"disabled"} works only at low, medium and high effort; at xhigh and max it returns a 400 error.
Omit temperature, top_p and top_k for Claude Haiku 5.5 (they can return an error) and guide behavior through prompting instead.
Assistant message prefill is rejected with a 400 error even with thinking off; end messages with a user turn and use structured outputs, tools with enum fields, or system-prompt instructions instead.

Thinking tokens count toward max_tokens (up to 128,000 synchronous output), so a max_tokens value sized for Haiku 4.5 without thinking can cut off the reply; leave room for thinking or lower effort. Select response content blocks by type, not position, because responses can begin with thinking blocks.

When giving the model a search tool, supply today's date in the system prompt or tool description; at low effort or with long system prompts, add a nudge that training data ends before today's date and to search for changeable facts. Avoid blanket 'always search' instructions, which caused searches on half of prompts needing none.

With thinking off and structured outputs (output_config.format), the model may skip a needed tool call; use adaptive thinking for such requests, remove output_config.format where a tool call is required, or force the call with tool_choice (forced tool_choice yields a response starting with the tool call and no thinking block).

In long coding-agent system prompts at low effort the model can stop early; add instructions to keep working until everything asked is done, and raise effort (low to medium roughly halved early stopping). At low and medium effort it may report code changes done without running a check, so instruct it to run a real check (tests, type-check, build) before reporting done.

Deliver mid-turn user messages as a user turn text block after the last tool_result, never inside a tool_result block, because the model is trained to resist prompt injection through tool results and may ignore it.

Keep conversations append-only (system, tools and earlier messages unchanged) when sending Haiku 5.5 thinking blocks back; changing earlier turns can return a 400 error (default on accounts created on or after August 31, 2026). Thinking blocks are valid only in the producing (or linked) account, and thinking text is omitted by default unless thinking.display is set to "summarized".

Claude Haiku 5.5 uses the newer tokenizer (about 30 percent more tokens than Haiku 4.5 for the same text), so recount tokens with model set to claude-haiku-5-5; minimum cacheable prompt length is 512 tokens; long prompts over 100,000 tokens are billed at higher prices.

Requests can return stop_reason "refusal" from safety classifiers (stop_details.category: cyber, frontier_llm, bio, general_harms); there is no server-side fallback, so handle refusals in the client and do not simply resend the same request.

Call the model with API ID `claude-fable-5` (Bedrock: `anthropic.claude-fable-5`). It has a 1M-token context window, 128K max output (synchronous Messages API), accepts text and images and outputs text, and its default effort is `high`. The page marks Claude Fable 5 as a legacy model (Claude Fable 5.1, `claude-fable-5-1`, is the current Fable model).

Thinking is adaptive only and always on for Claude Fable 5: the thinking docs state it rejects `thinking: {type: "disabled"}` (thinking cannot be turned off), and the prompting guide says it has no extended-thinking budgets (no `budget_tokens`) and returns summarized-only thinking output.

Use effort as the primary control for intelligence, latency, and cost: `high` as the default for most tasks, `xhigh` for the most capability-sensitive workloads, and `medium` or `low` for routine work. Lower effort levels still perform well and often exceed `xhigh` on prior models; reduce effort if a task completes but takes longer than needed.

Plan for longer turns: individual requests on hard tasks can run for many minutes at higher effort and autonomous runs can last hours, so adjust client timeouts, streaming, and progress indicators before migrating, and consider checking on runs asynchronously (for example via scheduled jobs) instead of blocking. To curb overplanning, instruct it to act once it has enough information, not re-derive established facts or narrate options it will not pursue, and give a recommendation rather than an exhaustive survey (excluding thinking blocks).

Steer behavior with brief instructions rather than enumerating each behavior: a short brevity instruction (lead with the outcome in the first sentence, be selective about what to include rather than compressing into fragments, abbreviations, or arrow chains) is as effective as listing each over-elaboration pattern. Un-steered, especially at higher effort, the model can over-elaborate (surveying unpursued options, long root-cause explanations, heavily structured PR descriptions, narrating comments).

For long autonomous runs, instruct the model to audit each progress claim against a tool result from the current session and to state plainly when something is unverified, failed, or skipped; Anthropic reports this nearly eliminated fabricated status reports in its testing.

Do not tell the model to echo, transcribe, or explain its internal reasoning in the response text: such instructions can trigger a `reasoning_extraction` refusal on Claude Fable 5, and server-side fallback with `fallbacks: "default"` does not retry `reasoning_extraction` refusals. Audit prompts and skills for show-your-thinking instructions; read structured `thinking` blocks instead, and short explanations or action summaries are still fine.

Claude Fable 5 runs safety classifiers (offensive cybersecurity, biology and life sciences, extraction of summarized thinking) that can return a normal response with `stop_reason: "refusal"` and `stop_details.category`. To re-route declined requests, set `fallbacks` (for example the string `"default"`) with the `server-side-fallback-2026-07-01` beta header, or use client-side fallback; the prompting guide names Claude Opus 4.8 as the fallback target.

For autonomous pipelines, add a system reminder that the user cannot answer mid-task, to proceed without asking on reversible actions that follow from the request, and to check the last paragraph before ending a turn (do the work now if it is a plan or promise). Pair it with a checkpoint instruction to pause only for destructive or irreversible actions, real scope changes, or input only the user can provide. This addresses rare early stops where the model ends a turn with a text-only statement of intent.

Avoid showing a remaining-token or context-budget countdown to the model, since it can trigger suggestions to start a new session or summarize and hand off; if the harness must show it, add a reassurance such as 'You have ample context remaining. Do not stop, summarize, or suggest a new session on account of context limits.'

Re-evaluate older scaffolding: skills and prompts written for prior models are often too prescriptive for Claude Fable 5 and can degrade output quality, so review and consider removing them if default performance is better. For parallel work, the model dispatches subagents more readily than prior models; give explicit guidance on when to delegate, prefer asynchronous orchestrator-subagent communication, and use separate fresh-context verifier subagents rather than self-critique for long-run verification.

For claude-opus-4-6, if the model over-explores or thinks extensively at higher effort, replace blanket instructions such as 'Default to using [tool]' or 'If in doubt, use [tool]' with targeted ones. claude-opus-4-6 and later models may escape JSON strings in tool call arguments slightly differently (for example Unicode or forward-slash escaping). Parse tool call input with a standard JSON parser, not as a raw string.

On claude-opus-4-6 the thinking display default is summarized, meaning thinking blocks return summarized thinking text. This differs from Claude Opus 4.7 and later, where thinking text is omitted unless the request opts in.

Without guidance, claude-opus-4-6 may take hard-to-reverse actions or actions affecting shared systems, such as deleting files, force-pushing, or posting to external services. Add prompt guidance that asks it to confirm before destructive or shared-system actions. It also tends to overengineer with extra files and abstractions, so add specific guidance to keep solutions minimal.

On Claude Opus 4.7, a request with no thinking field runs with thinking off. Set thinking: {"type": "adaptive"} to turn adaptive thinking on. thinking: {"type": "enabled", "budget_tokens": N} and thinking: {"type": "between_tools"} return a 400 error. thinking: {"type": "disabled"} is accepted (thinking stays off).

On Claude Opus 4.7, non-default temperature, top_p, or top_k values return a 400 error on every request, whether or not thinking is used. The top_p default is 0.99, so top_p of 1 returns a 400, and so does sending both temperature and top_p. Omit these parameters and steer behavior through prompting.

For Claude Opus 4.7, start with effort xhigh for coding and agentic work, use high as the minimum for most intelligence-sensitive workloads, step down to medium for cost-sensitive work, and use max only when evals show headroom at xhigh. The API default is high, so xhigh must be set explicitly via output_config.effort.

When running Claude Opus 4.7 at xhigh or max effort, set a large max_tokens so the model has room to think and act across subagents and tool calls. Starting at 64k tokens and tuning from there is a reasonable default.

Claude Opus 4.7 respects effort levels more strictly than Opus 4.6, especially at low and medium, scoping work to what was asked. If reasoning looks shallow on complex problems, raise effort rather than prompting around it. If effort must stay low for latency, add targeted guidance such as 'This task involves multistep reasoning. Think carefully before responding.' Pair low effort with explicit checklists for multi-section tasks.

On Claude Opus 4.7, thinking blocks still appear in responses but their thinking field is empty by default (display omitted; the signature still carries the encrypted thinking for multi-turn continuity). This is a silent change from Opus 4.6, which returned summarized thinking by default. Opt in explicitly (for example display: "summarized") to receive thinking text.

Claude Opus 4.7 introduced a new tokenizer that may use roughly 1x to 1.35x as many tokens for text as models before it. Increase max_tokens headroom (including compaction triggers), re-test client-side token estimates, and verify with the /v1/messages/count_tokens endpoint.

Claude Opus 4.7 gives more regular, higher-quality progress updates during long agentic traces. Scaffolding that forces interim status messages (for example 'After every 3 tool calls, summarize progress') can be tried without. Reasoning between tool calls appears in thinking blocks with adaptive thinking.
Claude Opus 4.7 rejects role: "system" messages inside the messages array with a 400 error and rejects speed: "fast" (fast mode) with an error; put instructions in the top-level system field.

Claude Opus 4.7 is the first Claude model with high-resolution image support: max image resolution is 2,576 pixels on the long edge (up from 1,568), which can use up to roughly 3x more image tokens per full-resolution image, so downsample if the fidelity is not needed. Pointing and bounding-box coordinates are 1:1 with actual image pixels, so no scale-factor conversion is needed.

Claude Opus 4.7 (claude-opus-4-7) is a legacy model released April 16, 2026, with a 1M-token context window, 128K max output tokens (300K on the Message Batches API with the output-300k-2026-03-24 beta header), adaptive thinking, and default effort high. Retirement is not sooner than April 16, 2027, and Anthropic recommends migrating to Claude Opus 5.5.

Start with the xhigh effort level for coding and agentic use cases on Claude Opus 4.8, and use a minimum of high effort for most intelligence-sensitive use cases. Low is reserved for short, scoped, latency-sensitive tasks that are not intelligence-sensitive.

On Claude Opus 4.8, thinking is off unless the request explicitly sets thinking: {type: "adaptive"}. Adaptive thinking is steerable by prompt: if the model thinks more often than wanted (for example with large system prompts), add guidance such as 'Thinking adds latency and should only be used when it will meaningfully improve answer quality... When in doubt, respond directly.'

Claude Opus 4.8 respects effort levels strictly, especially at the low end: at low and medium it scopes work to what was asked, so moderately complex tasks at low effort risk under-thinking. If reasoning is shallow, raise effort to high or xhigh rather than prompting around it; if effort must stay low for latency, add a targeted line such as 'This task involves multistep reasoning. Think carefully through the problem before responding.'

When running Claude Opus 4.8 at max or xhigh effort, set a large max output token budget (start at 64k tokens and tune from there) so the model has room to think and act across subagents and tool calls.

Claude Opus 4.8 calibrates response length to its estimate of task complexity (shorter on simple lookups, much longer on open-ended analysis) instead of a fixed verbosity. To change style, add explicit instructions such as 'Provide concise, focused responses. Skip non-essential context, and keep examples minimal.' Positive examples of the desired concision work better than negative instructions.

Claude Opus 4.8 favors reasoning over tool calls and spawns fewer subagents by default. Raising effort to high or xhigh substantially increases tool use; you can also explicitly describe when and how to use tools, and give explicit guidance on when subagents are desirable (for example, do not spawn a subagent for work doable in one response; fan out in the same turn across items or multiple files).

Claude Opus 4.8 interprets prompts literally and does not silently generalize an instruction from one item to another, particularly at lower effort. State scope explicitly when an instruction should apply broadly (for example, 'Apply this formatting to every section, not just the first one').

For code-review harnesses on Claude Opus 4.8, avoid severity or conservatism filters such as 'only report high-severity issues', 'be conservative', or 'don't nitpick', because the model follows them faithfully and may drop findings it did investigate, lowering measured recall. Instead ask it to report every issue with a confidence level and estimated severity and filter in a separate step, or, for single-pass filtering, state a concrete reporting threshold.

Claude Opus 4.8 uses more tokens in interactive multi-turn coding sessions because it reasons more after user turns. Use xhigh or high effort, specify task, intent, and constraints upfront in the first human turn, and reduce required user interactions; ambiguous prompts supplied progressively over many turns reduce token efficiency and sometimes performance.

Claude Opus 4.8 supports computer use via the computer_toolset_20260801 toolset and the computer_20251124 tool version, plus the browser use tool (browser_toolset_20260801), with a maximum image resolution of 2576px / 3.75MP; sending images at 1080p balances performance and cost.

Claude Opus 4.8 (model ID claude-opus-4-8 on the Claude API; anthropic.claude-opus-4-8 on Bedrock) has a 1M-token context window, 128K max output (300K on the Message Batches API with the output-300k-2026-03-24 beta header), adaptive thinking, and default effort high. It is a legacy model released May 28, 2026, with retirement not sooner than May 28, 2027; Anthropic recommends migrating to Claude Opus 5.5.

Migration notes from Claude Opus 4.8 to Opus 5.5: on Opus 4.8 thinking is off unless requested (a request with no thinking field runs without thinking), it accepts thinking: {type: "disabled"}, forced tool choice, and computer_20251124, and returns text between tool calls as text blocks. The minimum cacheable prompt length on Opus 4.8 is 1,024 tokens (512 on Opus 5.5), and Priority Tier is supported on Opus 4.8.

Claude Sonnet 4.5 is deprecated (deprecated September 30, 2026) and retires on the Claude API on November 30, 2026; the recommended replacement is claude-sonnet-5-5. Use the dated ID claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929 (alias claude-sonnet-4-5) and plan migration before the retirement date.

Claude Sonnet 4.5 has a 200K-token context window and a 64K-token max output on the synchronous Messages API; the 300K Message Batches output extension is not available for it, and it has no effort parameter (default effort: not supported).

On Claude Sonnet 4.5, a request with no thinking field runs with thinking off. Valid thinking.type values are "disabled" and "enabled" (extended thinking with budget_tokens); "adaptive" and "between_tools" return a 400 error.

Claude Sonnet 4.5 accepts a prefilled last assistant turn (Claude Sonnet 4.6 and later reject it with a 400 error), so prefill still works on this model but should be replaced with structured outputs, system-prompt instructions, or user-turn continuations when migrating.

Claude Sonnet 4.5 features context awareness, which lets the model track its remaining context window (token budget) during a conversation. In a harness that compacts context or saves state to files, tell the model so, otherwise it may try to wrap up work as it nears the context limit.

On Claude Sonnet 4.5, interleaved thinking between tool calls uses the beta header interleaved-thinking-2025-05-14, and fine-grained tool streaming uses the beta header fine-grained-tool-streaming-2025-05-14; both are removed or replaced (eager_input_streaming: true) when moving to Claude Sonnet 5.5.

Claude Sonnet 4.5 and later (4.5+) models keep trailing newlines in tool call string parameters and stop with the model_context_window_exceeded stop reason at the context window limit; handle the refusal stop reason as well.

Claude Sonnet 4.5 pricing is $3 / MTok input and $15 / MTok output, with cache reads at $0.30 / MTok, 5-minute cache writes at $3.75 / MTok and 1-hour cache writes at $6 / MTok; Batch API gives a 50% discount on input and output.
