gpt-6.1-terra accepts text and image input and produces text output only (no audio or video). It supports streaming, structured outputs, function calling, and prompt caching. Predicted outputs and fine-tuning are not supported. Context window is 1,050,000 tokens, max output is 128,000 tokens, and cached input costs 5% of the uncached input rate. Prompts over 272K input tokens are priced higher across the whole request.

The GPT-6 family prompt-guidance prompts are a starting point across the GPT-6 family, but the page says they address behavior observed with GPT-6 Astra and must be evaluated with the chosen model and workload. Do not assume Astra-specific behaviors, such as heavy use of lists and Markdown or the skills and AGENTS.md instruction-following note, apply to Terra.
Treat reasoning.effort as a tuning knob, not the primary way to recover quality. Supported values and defaults are model-dependent, so check the model page first.

max_output_tokens includes reasoning tokens as well as visible output. If the limit is hit, the response status is incomplete, possibly before any visible output. OpenAI recommends reserving at least 25,000 tokens for reasoning and output.

gemini-2.5-flash is deprecated: it is no longer selectable in Google AI Studio and API access is limited to existing users. Effective December 1, 2026 (earliest possible shutdown date), all API requests to gemini-2.5-flash automatically route to gemini-3.5-flash-lite and are billed at Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite rates. Set the model string to gemini-3.5-flash-lite before that date.
The gemini-2.5-flash model page lists a 1,048,576-token input limit and a 65,536-token output limit, with text, image, video and audio input and text-only output.

gemini-2.5-flash supports Batch API, Caching, Code execution, File search, Function calling, Search grounding, Grounding with Google Maps, Structured outputs, Thinking and URL context. It does not support Live API, audio generation or image generation.

Thinking is on by default for gemini-2.5-flash. The thinking guide controls thinking with the thinking_level parameter in generation_config, and lists low, medium and high as supported levels for this model.
The gemini-2.5-flash model page lists its knowledge cutoff as January 2025, so supply recent facts in the prompt or use search grounding or URL context for anything later.
For thinking models, response pricing is the sum of output tokens and thinking tokens. In stateless mode, resend all thought blocks exactly as received from the model.

Use the stable model ID gemini-2.5-flash-image (Nano Banana, original). The earlier gemini-2.5-flash-image-preview ID is deprecated (shutdown January 15, 2026), so migrate any code still pointing at the preview ID to the stable ID.

Plan a migration: gemini-2.5-flash-image is listed on the deprecations page with an earliest shutdown date of March 15, 2027 and gemini-3.1-flash-lite-image as the recommended replacement. The image-generation guide calls it the legacy model of the Nano Banana series and recommends Nano Banana 2 Lite for higher quality, faster speeds and lower pricing.

Do not request thinking, function calling, structured outputs, search grounding, URL context, code execution, context caching, or the Live API from this model. Its model page lists all of them as not supported. Supported: image generation and the Batch API, with image and text inputs and image and text outputs.

Budget for token limits of 65,536 input tokens and 32,768 output tokens, with a June 2025 knowledge cutoff. Position the model for high-volume generation and conversational image editing where speed and efficiency matter.

Limit input to about 3 reference images: the Limitations section says gemini-2.5-flash-image works best with up to 3 images as input. The 14-image and multi-character or multi-object fidelity guidance applies to other models (Gemini 3 Pro Image, Nano Banana 2.1, Gemini 3.1 Flash Image), not to this one.

Choose output shape by aspect ratio. This model offers fixed sizes at a flat 1290 tokens per image: 1:1 1024x1024, 2:3 832x1248, 3:2 1248x832, 3:4 864x1184, 4:3 1184x864, 4:5 896x1152, 5:4 1152x896, 9:16 768x1344, 16:9 1344x768, 21:9 1536x672. The 1:4, 4:1 and 1:8 style ratios and the 1K/2K/4K image-size options are documented for newer models, not for this one.

Do not rely on an exact output image count: the model will not always follow the exact number of image outputs requested. Audio input is not supported, and video input is documented only for newer Nano Banana models.

For images that contain text, generate the text first and then ask for an image that includes that text. For best performance use the listed languages: EN, Arabic (Egypt), German, Spanish (Mexico), French, Hindi, Indonesian, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese (Brazil), Russian, Ukrainian, Vietnamese, Chinese (Simplified).

For editing, supply the source image with a text description of the change. The page says the model will match the original image's style, lighting and perspective, and that a mask can be defined conversationally to edit only part of an image. Make sure you have the necessary rights to any images you upload.
Expect all generated images to carry a SynthID watermark.
Call the model with the code gemini-2.5-flash-lite (stable). The preview code gemini-2.5-flash-lite-preview-09-2025 is shut down and must not be used.

Size requests to the documented limits: input token limit 1,048,576 and output token limit 65,536. Accepted inputs are text, image, video, audio and PDF; output is text only (no audio or image generation, no Live API).

The model supports Batch API, caching, code execution, file search, flex inference, function calling, Grounding with Google Maps, priority inference, search grounding, structured outputs, thinking and URL context, so these tool and API features can be used with it.

Thinking is Off by default for gemini-2.5-flash-lite, unlike gemini-2.5-flash and gemini-2.5-pro which are On. To get reasoning, set a thinking level explicitly; the thinking page lists low, medium and high as the supported levels for this model.

The thinking page controls thinking through the thinking_level parameter; it does not document thinking_budget (0 to disable or -1 for dynamic) for this model, so do not assume budget semantics from this page.
When thinking is turned on, response pricing is the sum of output tokens and thinking tokens; read total thinking tokens from the total_thought_tokens field when budgeting cost.
For a stateless tool-using flow, resend the tool result signatures (including those for built-in tools such as Google Search) in subsequent turns.

Always include few-shot examples in prompts, keep their structure and formatting identical, and do not include too many because the model may overfit to the examples. Instructions can be removed if the examples already show the task clearly.

Give clear, specific instructions, state constraints and the desired response format, supply the needed context rather than assuming the model has it, and for complex JSON schemas use the API's structured output feature. Break complex prompts into one prompt per instruction.
The model's knowledge cutoff is January 2025, so enable search grounding when recent or obscure facts are needed.

Access to the 2.5 models is limited to users who have actively used them before. gemini-2.5-flash-lite is not deprecated and is served until further notice, but for new projects the page recommends 3.5 Flash-Lite or 3.8 Flash.
Control reasoning on this model with thinkingBudget (a thinking token budget); thinkingLevel is the setting for the 3.x Live models, not for 2.5 Flash Live.
Affective dialog is supported on Gemini 2.5 Flash Live only: set enable_affective_dialog to true in the session config and use the v1beta API version.
Proactive audio is configurable on Gemini 2.5 Flash Live: set proactive_audio to true inside the proactivity config under v1beta so the model can decide not to respond to irrelevant input.

The model supports function calling, search grounding, thinking and audio generation, and does not support caching, code execution, structured outputs, URL context, file search, Google Maps grounding, image generation or the Batch API; do not plan on those features. Limits: 131,072 input tokens and 8,192 output tokens.

Native audio output models only support the AUDIO response modality; to get text, enable output_audio_transcription in the setup config (the transcription language is inferred from the model's response).
Native audio models choose the output language automatically and do not accept an explicit language code; restrict the languages the model speaks through the system instructions instead.

Function calling on 2.5 Flash Live supports both synchronous and asynchronous calls; send_client_content is supported throughout the conversation for incremental content updates, and each server event carries only one content part.

Input audio is raw little-endian 16-bit PCM (16 kHz default, other rates allowed if declared in the MIME type) and output is always 24 kHz PCM; the native audio context window is 128k tokens, and audio-only sessions are limited to 15 minutes (audio plus video 2 minutes) unless session management or context compression is used.

The model waits for user input at session start, so include a greeting prompt or trigger content to make it speak first; add an explicit output-language directive in the system instruction, order the system instruction persona then conversation rules then guardrails, and describe each tool step in its own sentence.
Native audio accumulates about 25 tokens per second, so enable context compression for long sessions; keep the latest session resumption token (valid 2 hours) and handle GoAway timeLeft to reconnect.
Send text only as input and expect audio only as output; the model is a text-to-speech model whose supported capability is audio generation.
Keep each request within the model's token limits: input is capped at 8,192 tokens and output at 16,384 tokens.

Do not rely on thinking, function calling, structured outputs, code execution, caching, Batch API, Live API, Search grounding, URL context, file search, Google Maps grounding or image generation with this model; the model page lists all of them as not supported.

Use this model for low-latency, cost-efficient speech synthesis such as real-time assistants, high-volume narration and conversational use cases, where fine-grained control over voice style and pacing is needed.

Plan migration: the deprecations page lists gemini-2.5-flash-preview-tts (released May 20, 2025) with a shutdown date of November 17, 2026 (stated as the earliest possible date) and recommends gemini-3.8-flash-tts or gemini-3.8-flash-lite-tts as replacements.

Do not apply the Gemini 3.8 TTS prompting pattern (Interactions API with response_format and generation_config.speech_config, style in speech_metadata.style, text as verbatim transcript) to this model. The current speech guide says earlier preview models, including gemini-2.5-pro-preview-tts, take stage directions embedded in plain text, and it does not document the 2.5 Flash TTS API shape.

Call the model with the model string `gemini-2.5-pro`. It accepts audio, images, video, text and PDF as input and produces text only, with a 1,048,576-token input limit and a 65,536-token output limit.

gemini-2.5-pro supports Batch API, caching, code execution, file search, Flex and Priority inference, function calling, Search grounding, Grounding with Google Maps, structured outputs, thinking and URL context. It does not support audio generation, image generation or the Live API, so do not request those from it.

gemini-2.5-pro is deprecated and no longer selectable in Google AI Studio, and API access is limited to existing users. Effective December 1, 2026, requests to gemini-2.5-pro are automatically routed to gemini-3.8-flash and billed at Gemini 3.8 Flash rates, so update the model string before that date and review the Gemini 3.8 Flash migration guide.

When migrating off gemini-2.5-pro, the page lists these breaking changes. Function calling and thought_signature validation change. thinking_level replaces thinking_budget. Sampling parameters are removed. Prefilled model turns are no longer supported. Do not carry prefilled model turns or sampling-parameter tuning over to the replacement.

On thinking models, max_output_tokens counts thought tokens as well as the visible response. If the limit is reached during reasoning, the response can be truncated or empty, and the thinking tokens are still billed. Set the output cap with the thinking overhead in mind.

Thinking tokens are billed together with output tokens, on the full thoughts generated rather than only the returned summaries. For gemini-2.5-pro the pricing page labels the output price row as including thinking tokens, so budget cost on output plus thinking.

Match thinking effort to task difficulty. Use minimal thinking for simple tasks such as fact retrieval or classification, default thinking for moderate tasks, and maximum thinking for complex tasks such as advanced coding or math. For lengthy outputs, prompt the model to think less to save tokens. Thought summaries are off by default and can be enabled to review failures and refine prompts.

For gemini-2.5-pro, context caching (standard paid tier) is priced at $0.125 per 1M tokens for prompts up to 200k tokens and $0.25 above 200k, plus $4.50 per 1M tokens per hour of storage. It is not available on the free tier. Reuse large repeated prefixes through caching.

Prompts over 200k tokens are priced at a higher tier for gemini-2.5-pro. Standard is $2.50 input and $15.00 output per 1M tokens, against $1.25 and $10.00 at or below 200k. Keep prompts at or under 200k tokens where possible to avoid the higher rate.
Model gemini-2.5-pro-preview-tts takes text input only and produces audio output only; input token limit is 8,192 and output token limit is 16,384.

Do not rely on Thinking, Function calling, Structured outputs, Caching, Search grounding, Code execution, URL context or the Live API with gemini-2.5-pro-preview-tts: the model page lists all of these as not supported. Supported: audio generation and the Batch API.
gemini-2.5-pro-preview-tts is positioned for long-form content, professional narration and complex creative workflows (studio-quality speech synthesis).

gemini-2.5-pro-preview-tts has a listed earliest shutdown date of November 17, 2026, with recommended replacements gemini-3.8-flash-tts or gemini-3.8-flash-lite-tts; plan migration, since the page says these are the earliest possible retirement dates and exact dates will be communicated in advance.
gemini-2.5-pro-preview-tts supports single-speaker and multi-speaker generation but not voice design, voice replication or voice remixing (those require the Gemini 3.8 TTS models).

When migrating from gemini-2.5-pro-preview-tts to Gemini 3.8 TTS, separate delivery style from the transcript: put acting and pacing directions in the speech metadata style field, keep the text as a verbatim transcript with inline tags, send each speaker line as its own content item with a speaker label, use angle-bracket inline vocal tags such as laugh or short pause, each written inside angle brackets, and expect default audio/wav output on unary requests.

Set reasoning effort for gemini-3-flash-preview with thinking_level; the supported values are minimal, low, medium and high. The model thinks by default at high ('On (high)'), so set a lower level explicitly when you want lower cost or latency.

Do not set max_output_tokens too low on a thinking model. The model can stop while it is still reasoning and return truncated or empty output. To cut cost or latency, lower thinking_level instead of squeezing max_output_tokens.

Match thinking effort to the task. Use minimal for simple lookups or classification, the default for moderate comparisons, and maximum effort for advanced coding, math or multi-step planning. For lengthy outputs, prompt the model to think less to save tokens.

Thought summaries are off by default for this model (only the final output is returned). Set thinking_summaries to 'auto' to receive them, then read them to understand failures and refine prompts. Write client code that tolerates a thought step with a signature but an empty or missing summary.

In stateless Interactions API use, resend all thought blocks and built-in tool steps (for example Google Search) unchanged in the history, and do not remove or modify them. In stateful mode (store: true with previous_interaction_id) the server preserves signatures automatically.

For function calling with Gemini 3 series models (the series gemini-3-flash-preview belongs to), the SDKs handle thought signatures automatically. In stateless mode, pass back all model-generated steps from the earlier turn, including thought and function_call steps, exactly as received. Gemini 3 series models can also take multimodal content in function response parts and can combine built-in tools with function calling in Interactions.

gemini-3-flash-preview takes text, image, video, audio and PDF input and returns text only. Its input limit is 1,048,576 tokens and its output limit is 65,536 tokens. It supports function calling, structured outputs, code execution, search grounding, URL context, computer use, caching, batch, flex and priority inference, file search and Maps grounding. It does not support the Live API or audio or image generation.

Use gemini-3-pro-image (Nano Banana Pro) for complex visual tasks that need advanced reasoning, brand consistency and high-fidelity text rendering; it is optimized for professional asset production (graphic design, product mockups, factual data visualizations). Flash-based image models are the speed and volume option.

Thinking is always on for Gemini 3 image models: it is enabled by default and cannot be disabled in the API. The model may generate up to two interim images to test composition, and the last image within Thinking is also the final rendered image. The thinking-levels table lists only Nano Banana 2.1 and Gemini 3.1 Flash (Lite) Image, so no thinking-level control is documented for Pro. Thinking tokens are billed by default.

Reference images: Nano Banana models accept up to 14 reference images in total. For the Pro column the documented limits are up to 6 high-fidelity object images, up to 5 character images for consistency, and up to 3 style-reference images. Style references are not offered by the other Nano Banana models.

Output size: Gemini 3 image models default to 1K output. Pro supports 1K, 2K and 4K. Set image_size with an uppercase K (for example "2K" or "4K"); lowercase values such as "1k" are rejected. The 512px size is for Gemini 3.1 Flash Image only.

gemini-3-pro-image can produce interleaved text and images in a single response; convenience properties such as .output_image will not capture the full sequence, so iterate over the response steps/parts instead.

Model card facts for gemini-3-pro-image: stable id gemini-3-pro-image; inputs are image and text, outputs are image and text; input limit 65,536 tokens, output limit 32,768 tokens. Supported: Batch API, image generation, search grounding, thinking. Not supported: function calling, structured outputs, code execution, URL context, file search, Google Maps grounding, caching, Live API, flex and priority inference. Search grounding is the only supported tool.

Lifecycle and migration: the preview id gemini-3-pro-image-preview launched 2025-11-20; gemini-3-pro-image (Nano Banana Pro) went GA on 2026-05-28, and gemini-3-pro-image-preview was deprecated with shutdown on 2026-06-25. Calls should use the GA id gemini-3-pro-image (the changelog does not name it explicitly as the replacement).

Text-in-image prompting: for accurate text rendering use Gemini 3 Pro Image, and describe the font style descriptively in the prompt. For comic or storyboard sequences that need accurate text and storytelling, the guide says the prompts work best with Gemini 3 Pro and Gemini 3.1 Flash Image.

For iterative image edits the guide recommends multi-turn conversation; in the Interactions API turns are chained with previous_interaction_id, and the thought-signatures page says the Interactions API manages reasoning (thought signatures) at the API level. The fetched pages do not state signature requirements specifically for gemini-3-pro-image.
Use the stable model id gemini-3.1-flash-image (Nano Banana 2). Only the stable version is listed; no preview or dated variant is documented on the per-model page.
Plan for a 131,072-token input limit and a 32,768-token output limit. Accepted inputs are text, image, video and PDF; outputs are image and text.

Do not rely on function calling, structured outputs, code execution, URL context, Google Maps grounding, caching, the Live API, or Flex/Priority inference for this model. The per-model page lists all of these as unsupported. Supported are the Batch API, image generation, Search grounding and thinking.

Set output size with image_size. Valid values are 512px (0.5K, unique to Gemini 3.1 Flash Image among the Gemini 3 image models), 1K, 2K and 4K, with 1K the default. Labels must be uppercase because lowercase values such as 1k are rejected. The model also adds aspect ratios 1:4, 4:1, 1:8 and 8:1.

Thinking is on by default and cannot be disabled in the API for Gemini 3 image models. Gemini 3.1 Flash Image accepts thinking_level values minimal and high, with minimal the default. Set it in generation_config. Thinking tokens are billed, and the model may produce up to two interim images, the last of which is the final image.
Reference-image budget for this model: up to 10 object images for fidelity, up to 4 characters for resemblance, and up to 14 reference images in total. No style-reference allowance is listed for it.
Video input is supported for image generation on Gemini 3.1 Flash Image (and Nano Banana 2.1 and Flash Lite Image). Audio input is not supported.
Sequential-art prompts (comic panels, storyboards) work best with Gemini 3 Pro Image and Gemini 3.1 Flash Image, because of their text accuracy and storytelling ability.
Do not expect the model to honor an exact requested number of output images. For text rendered in images, first generate the text, then ask for an image containing it.

Prompt for images by being specific, stating the image's purpose as context, iterating conversationally with small follow-up edits, breaking complex scenes into ordered steps, describing the wanted scene positively (semantic negative prompts) instead of listing exclusions, and using photographic terms (wide-angle, macro) for camera control. The page states these as general best practices, not for one model.

On Vertex AI, gemini-3.1-flash-image supports GenerateContent and Count Tokens but not the Interactions API, Live API or Chat Completions. It supports implicit context caching, Google Search grounding and multi-turn image editing, but not function calling, structured output, code execution, URL context or tuning. Defaults are temperature 1.0 (range 0.0-2.0) and topP 0.95, with candidateCount fixed at 1.

On Vertex AI, plan image budgets with 14 images max per prompt, 1,120 tokens per input image, and output tokens of 747 at 512, 1,120 at 1K, 1,680 at 2K and 2,520 at 4K. Input formats are PNG, JPEG, WebP, HEIC and HEIF.

Call the model with the stable id gemini-3.1-flash-lite. The preview id gemini-3.1-flash-lite-preview was shut down on May 25, 2026 (GA released May 7, 2026), so migrate any requests using the preview id to the stable id.

Use gemini-3.1-flash-lite for straightforward, high-volume, low-latency, cost-sensitive tasks (translation, audio transcription, lightweight agentic tasks with structured JSON output, document parsing and summarization, model routing); the page says it 'is best at handling straightforward tasks at significant scale', so route harder tasks to a larger model.
Plan around the documented limits: input up to 1,048,576 tokens, output up to 65,536 tokens; inputs may be text, image, video, audio and PDF, but output is text only.

Do not rely on Live API, computer use, image generation or audio generation with this model; the model page lists them as not supported. Supported: function calling, structured outputs, thinking, code execution, search grounding, Grounding with Google Maps, URL context, file search, caching, Batch API, Flex and Priority inference.

Control reasoning through the thinking config (e.g. thinking_level='high') so the model spends extra compute on internal reasoning before the final output, for tasks that benefit from step-by-step reasoning. The model page does not document the default level or the supported level list for this model, so set thinking_level explicitly and test rather than assuming a default.
For output-only tasks such as translation, constrain the output with a system instruction; the model page's example uses 'Only output the translated text'.
The model suits a cheap classifier/router in front of larger models: the model page says the Gemini CLI uses Flash-Lite to classify task complexity and route to Flash or Pro accordingly.

To cut cost or latency on thinking models, lower thinking_level (low or medium) instead of setting a small max_output_tokens, and use minimal thinking for fact retrieval or classification. The page frames this as general guidance but its model table has no row for gemini-3.1-flash-lite, so apply it as a candidate.
Thinking is supported at levels minimal and high only, with minimal as the default; set it with thinking_level to trade quality against latency.

Thinking cannot be disabled in the API for Gemini 3 image models, and thinking tokens are billed by default; the model may generate up to two interim images to test composition, and the last thought image is the final rendered image.
Input limit is 65,536 tokens and output limit is 4,096 tokens. Inputs can be text, image, video and PDF; outputs are image and text. Audio inputs are not supported for image generation.

Not supported on this model: search grounding (including Grounding with Google Search), function calling, structured outputs, code execution, URL context, caching, file search, Live API, flex and priority inference. Do not rely on these in requests. Batch API is supported.

Video-to-image generation is supported: pass a public YouTube URL or an uploaded video file as multimodal context. Video inputs are only supported for Nano Banana 2.1, Gemini 3.1 Flash Image and Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite Image.
Migration: gemini-2.5-flash-image is legacy and the recommended migration path is Nano Banana 2 Lite (gemini-3.1-flash-lite-image), for higher quality, speed and lower price.

Prompt with detail and purpose: describe the subject concretely, state what the image is for, use photographic and cinematic terms for composition, and describe the scene positively instead of negating (for example 'an empty, deserted street' instead of 'no cars').

For complex scenes, break the prompt into steps (background, then foreground, then details) and iterate conversationally with small changes rather than expecting a perfect first image. The model will not always return the exact number of images requested.

To render text in an image, first generate the text, then ask for an image containing that text. For best results use the languages listed on the page (EN, ar-EG, de-DE, es-MX, fr-FR, hi-IN, id-ID, it-IT, ja-JP, ko-KR, pt-BR, ru-RU, ua-UA, vi-VN, zh-CN). All generated images carry a SynthID watermark.

Set reasoning with thinkingConfig.thinkingLevel (minimal, low, medium, high) instead of thinkingBudget; the default is minimal, chosen to optimize for lowest latency, so raise the level only when more reasoning is needed.
Function calling is synchronous only: the model does not respond until the client sends the tool response. Async function calling (NON_BLOCKING behavior, scheduling) is not supported on this model.
The client must handle tool calls manually and reply with a list of FunctionResponse objects; the Live API does not answer tool calls automatically.
Google Search grounding is supported through the session configuration; Google Maps grounding, code execution and URL context are not supported on this model.
Do not configure proactive audio or affective dialogue on this model (not yet supported); remove those settings when migrating from gemini-2.5-flash-native-audio-preview-12-2025.
A single BidiGenerateContentServerContent event can contain multiple parts (for example audio chunks plus transcript), so client code must process every part in each event rather than only the first.

Use send_client_content to add text or structured context mid-session and to seed history (initial_history_in_client_content in history_config); use send_realtime_input to stream text, audio or video.

Caching, Batch API, structured outputs, code execution, file search, image generation and URL context are not supported; token limits are 131,072 input and 65,536 output; inputs are text, images, audio and outputs are text and audio.
The model is a legacy preview; for new and production apps Google recommends migrating to gemini-3.8-live, or gemini-3.8-live-extended-thinking when more background reasoning is needed.

For Live API system instructions, write one per agent ordered as persona, conversational rules, guardrails; list rules in the order the model should follow them, describe each tool step in its own sentence, state conditions for invoking each tool, give if-x-then-y guardrail examples, and give an explicit output-language instruction. Prefer prompt chaining over long prompts, and add a prompt telling the model to greet the user first because the Live API waits for user input.
Treat gemini-3.1-flash-tts-preview as a legacy preview model: for new and production workloads, migrate to gemini-3.8-flash-tts (quality) or gemini-3.8-flash-lite-tts (high volume, low cost).
Send text-only input and expect audio-only output. Input token limit is 8,192 and output token limit is 16,384 for this model.

Do not rely on thinking, function calling, structured outputs, caching, code execution, search grounding, URL context, or the Live API with this model; the per-model page lists all of them as not supported. Audio generation and the Batch API are supported.
The model supports expressive audio tags for controlling narration (steerable prompts); the per-model page refers to the Text-to-Speech guide's controllable-speech section for syntax.
Both single-speaker and multi-speaker generation are supported by 3.1 Flash TTS Preview, but voice design, voice replication and voice remixing are not supported for it.
Multi-speaker generation supports at most 2 speakers using prebuilt voices (limitation stated for TTS multi-speaker requests on the speech generation page).

On unary requests this model returns headerless raw PCM (audio/l16) by default, unlike the 3.8 models which return WAV; handle or decode raw PCM accordingly, and set audio/l16 explicitly in a 3.8 migration if the pipeline expects headerless audio.

Earlier preview models including 3.1 took stage directions embedded in plain text, and multi-speaker scripts as 'Speaker: ...' prefixes in one text block; when migrating to 3.8, move acting and pacing directions into speech_metadata.style and use one content item per speaker turn.
Gemini 3.1 Pro (gemini-3.1-pro-preview) supports thinking_level values low, medium and high; minimal is not offered for this model.
The default thinking setting for gemini-3.1-pro-preview is On (high); lower thinking_level to reduce cost or latency.

max_output_tokens counts thought tokens, so a low limit can truncate responses; the page recommends lowering thinking_level instead to cut cost or latency. Billing is based on the full thought tokens generated, not just the returned summary.

In stateless use of the Interactions API, all thought blocks (with their signatures) must be resent exactly as received; in stateful mode (store true with previous_interaction_id) the server manages signatures. Thought summaries are opt-in via thinking_summaries.
gemini-3.1-pro-preview takes text, image, video, audio and PDF input and returns text only, with 1,048,576 input and 65,536 output token limits.

gemini-3.1-pro-preview supports function calling, structured outputs, code execution, search grounding, URL context, file search, caching and the Batch API; it does not support the Live API, image generation or audio generation.

For agentic work that mixes bash with custom tools (for example view_file and search_code), use the variant gemini-3.1-pro-preview-customtools, which prioritizes custom tools but may show quality fluctuations in use cases that do not benefit from such tools.

Gemini 3 models respond best to direct, well-structured prompts that define the task and constraints, and are direct and efficient by default, so conversational or detailed output must be requested explicitly. The page is written for Gemini 3 models and does not name 3.1 Pro.

For long context with Gemini 3, supply all context first and put the specific question or instructions at the very end, using a clear transition phrase; put behavioral constraints, persona and output format in the system instruction or at the start of the user prompt.
For earlier Gemini 3 models, keep temperature, top_p and top_k at their default values to avoid degraded reasoning performance (Gemini 4 and 3.6+ models ignore them).

Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview has a minimum of 4,096 input tokens for caching; implicit caching is on by default for Gemini 2.5 and newer models, and placing large common content at the start of the prompt and sending similar-prefix requests close together improves cache hits.

Call this model only through the Live API as a continuous audio-to-audio interpreter pipeline; it does not wait for conversational turns, and it supports no tools, function calling, Google Search, or system instructions, so do not try to steer it with a prompt.

Enable translation by adding translationConfig inside the session generation config, with responseModalities set to ["AUDIO"] and translationConfig.targetLanguageCode set to a BCP-47 code (default "en"; variants such as pt-BR, pt-PT, zh-Hans, zh-Hant).

Set translationConfig.echoTargetLanguage to control speech already in the target language: true echoes it back, false (default) keeps the model silent for it. With echo true, background noise or music may add artifacts to the translated audio.

Input must be raw 16-bit little-endian mono PCM at 16kHz with MIME type audio/pcm;rate=16000, sent in 100ms chunks for low latency; output is raw 16-bit mono PCM at 24kHz. Text input is not supported.

To receive transcripts, add inputAudioTranscription and outputAudioTranscription (empty objects) to the session config; read them from serverContent.inputTranscription and serverContent.outputTranscription, and read translated audio from serverContent.modelTurn.parts[].inlineData.

The model page lists these as not supported for gemini-3.5-live-translate-preview: thinking, function calling, structured outputs, caching, code execution, search grounding, Maps grounding, file search, URL context, Batch API, Flex and Priority inference. Do not send thinking settings or tool declarations.
Token limits for this model are 131,072 input and 65,536 output; it is preview-only and handles audio input with audio plus text (transcript) output.

In client-side apps use ephemeral tokens on the v1beta endpoint: include translationConfig in liveConnectConstraints to lock the target language, or omit it and set lock_additional_fields to [] so the client can choose the target language.

Expect limitations: input language detection can struggle with heavy accents, similar languages (e.g. Spanish vs Portuguese) and rapid switching (mainly affecting the input transcript); output voice replication is inconsistent (voice may shift after pauses, be assigned the wrong gender, or stick on one voice in rapid multi-speaker talk); noise and music are filtered but not all background audio is ignored.

Use model ID gemini-3.5-transcribe for unary (file) transcription of prerecorded audio; use the separate ID gemini-3.5-transcribe-live for real-time streaming over the Live API (WebSockets). In REST it appears as models/gemini-3.5-transcribe.

Call the model through the Interactions API (a POST to the v1beta interactions endpoint on generativelanguage.googleapis.com, or client.interactions.create in the SDKs), uploading audio first with the Files API and passing the file as input. The transcription guide documents only the Interactions API for this model and does not mention generateContent.

Control transcription through generation_config.transcription_config (camelCase transcriptionConfig in JavaScript), not through a prompt: the guide documents no prompt or system-instruction field for transcription. Fields are language_codes, custom_vocabulary and mode.

Set transcription_config.language_codes (BCP-47, for example es-ES) when the language is known; omit it or pass [] for automatic detection, which also handles intra- and inter-sentence code-switching across 85+ languages.

mode defaults to verbatim (word-for-word, keeps filler words, repetitions and false starts). Set mode to "smart" for a reading-optimized transcript that removes disfluencies, resolves spoken self-corrections and applies formatting (lists, dates, currencies, numbers). Timestamps and diarization require verbatim mode; smart mode cannot be combined with timestamps or diarization.

For word timing use mode = {"type":"verbatim","timestamp_granularities":["word"]}; for speaker labels use mode.diarization_mode = "speaker" (up to 8 speakers; attribution for 3 or more speakers is experimental). Word data is returned in steps[].content[].annotations[] with type word_info (text, speaker, start_offset, end_offset). Word-level timestamps may degrade overall transcription accuracy, so enable them only when needed.

custom_vocabulary accepts up to 1,000 terms to bias recognition, with best results at about 100 or fewer distinctive terms (not common words). It cannot be combined with diarization or word timestamps, and the API rejects requests that try.

Unary requests accept audio up to 1 hour, reduced to 30 minutes when speaker diarization or word-level timestamps are enabled; the live model is limited to 10 minutes per session. Supported input MIME types include wav, mp3, aiff, aac, ogg, flac, mpeg, m4a, l16, opus, alaw, mulaw and webm; use the Files API for recordings longer than a few seconds and prefer clean recordings without severe clipping.

The model page lists thinking, function calling, caching, code execution, file search and image generation as not supported, and Batch API, Flex inference and Priority inference as not available consumption options, so do not set thinking or tool configuration or rely on context caching or batch mode for this model.

The live model gemini-3.5-transcribe-live does not support word-level timestamps or speaker diarization; those are file-endpoint features only, while language auto-detection, custom vocabulary (up to 1,000 terms) and smart dictation/formatting work on both endpoints.

Call gemini-3.5-transcribe-live through the Live API (Google Gen AI SDK client.aio.live.connect, ai.live.connect in JavaScript, or a raw WebSocket BidiGenerateContent setup message with model 'models/gemini-3.5-transcribe-live') and set response modalities to TEXT. It is a dedicated low-latency speech recognition pipeline, not a conversational agent.
Send audio as raw 16-bit PCM, 16 kHz, mono, little-endian with MIME type audio/pcm;rate=16000, in roughly 100 ms chunks (1,024 to 2,048 frames), and signal the end of input with audio_stream_end.
Leave language_codes omitted or empty ([]) to have the model auto-detect language and handle multilingual speech; pass BCP-47 hints such as es-ES or fr-FR only to bias recognition.

Choose the transcription mode explicitly: VERBATIM (default) gives a literal transcript including filler words and false starts; SMART removes disfluencies and applies formatting, grammar and casing. SMART mode cannot be combined with word annotations.

Render interim_input_transcription (speculative partial hypotheses updated while the speaker talks) for live subtitles, and store input_transcription (the finalized transcript emitted on pause or turn completion) as the committed text.

Voice activity detection has three modes: automatic server-side (default), hybrid (server speech-start detection plus a client audioStreamEnd signal for faster finalization), and manual push-to-talk (set automatic_activity_detection.disabled to true and send activity_start/activity_end).
Live transcription sessions support continuous streaming for up to 10 minutes per session, so long audio must be split across sessions.

Speaker diarization and word-level timestamps are not supported on gemini-3.5-transcribe-live (only utterance-level timestamps are emitted); use the non-streaming gemini-3.5-transcribe model for speaker labels or word timing.
For browser or mobile clients, create a short-lived ephemeral token on the server with auth_tokens.create, constrained via live_connect_constraints to this model, rather than shipping an API key.

Call gemini-3.8-flash-lite-tts through the Interactions API (client.interactions.create or POST /v1beta/interactions) with response_format={"type": "audio"}; speech_config takes an array for one speaker (e.g. [{"voice": "Kore"}]) and an object with speakers for multiple speakers.

Treat the text field as a verbatim transcript: put delivery direction and speaker labels in speech_metadata (speaker and style on each text block or part), not inline in the text, because inline directions such as 'Say cheerfully:' may be read aloud.

Use angle-bracket tags (for example short pause, sigh and laugh, each written inside angle brackets) only for momentary vocal events and pauses; put sustained styles such as whispering in speech_metadata.style. Keep tags to human vocalizations and write them in English even for non-English transcripts.

Do not rely on this model for features it does not support: the model page lists thinking, function calling, structured outputs, caching, Live API, search grounding and code execution as not supported; supported are audio generation, Batch API, Flex inference and Priority inference.

Input is text only with an 8,192-token limit, and output is audio with a 16,384-token limit (Gemini API serving limit); split long responses into shorter turns, with one TTS call per turn for voice agents and without resending a long persona.

Unary requests return WAV (audio/wav, 24 kHz mono 16-bit PCM with a 44-byte RIFF header) by default, unlike gemini-3.1-flash-tts-preview which returned headerless PCM; remove manual WAV wrapping, or request audio/l16, audio/mulaw or audio/alaw (AUDIO_L16 etc. in generateContent) for headerless output. Streaming returns headerless audio/l16 by default; sample_rate accepts 24000, 16000 or 8000.

In multi-speaker requests set speaker on every turn, matching a configured speaker; a single request supports at most 2 speakers and only with prebuilt voices (for custom voices, synthesize each turn separately and concatenate the audio).

Replace long style blocks with a custom designed voice (reference its voice_... ID) and a minimal or empty style string; do not put age, gender or permanent accent in style, and avoid meta-instructions like 'maintain identical timbre', which tend to increase voice drift.

Prompt by writing transcripts as people speak (natural disfluencies), test plain synthesis with empty style first, then add short style strings only where needed; pacing can also come from punctuation, ellipses and dashes, and capitalized words add emphasis.

Gemini 3.8 TTS treats the text field strictly as a verbatim transcript, so inline directions such as 'Say cheerfully:' or 'Speaker 1:' may be read aloud. Put delivery direction in speech_metadata.style and speaker in speech_metadata.speaker instead of in the text.

Use angle-bracket tags (laugh, sigh, cough, breath, short pause and long pause, each written inside angle brackets) inline only for momentary vocal events and pauses; put sustained delivery (whispering, pacing, volume, emotion) in speech_metadata.style. Stick to human vocalizations rather than non-vocal sound effects, and use English tags even in non-English text.

In multi-speaker requests, each turn must be its own content item carrying speech_metadata.speaker matching a configured speaker; do not use 'Speaker:' prefixes inside one text block. A single request supports at most 2 speakers and only with prebuilt voices; to mix custom voices, synthesize each speaker's turn separately and concatenate.

Unary requests return audio/wav with a RIFF header (24 kHz, mono, 16-bit PCM) by default, unlike earlier TTS models that returned headerless audio/l16 PCM; do not add your own WAV header. Set response_format.mime_type to audio/l16, audio/mulaw or audio/alaw (AUDIO_L16/AUDIO_MULAW/AUDIO_ALAW in generateContent) for headerless formats; streamed chunks (stream: true) are headerless raw 16-bit LE PCM at 24 kHz mono.

Limits and unsupported features: text input up to 8,192 tokens, audio output up to 16,384 tokens; supports Batch API, Flex and Priority inference; does NOT support thinking, function calling, structured outputs, caching, search grounding, code execution, or Live API, so do not set thinking or tool parameters.

Start with an empty style and add a short style string only for turns that need adjustment. Avoid meta-instructions telling the model to hold the voice steady (they increase drift), and do not put immutable traits (age, gender, names, permanent accent) in style; choose a suitable voice or use Voice design for persistent personas instead of long Audio Profile/Director's Notes blocks.

For natural pacing use commas, dashes and ellipses for hesitation, pause tags for exact timing, and style for overall speaking rate; capitalize specific words to add stress; write text as a realistic spoken transcript including disfluencies where appropriate.
For voice agents, make one TTS call per turn, keep style empty or a single short constant string, and split long responses into shorter turns.

Choose gemini-3.8-flash-tts over gemini-3.8-flash-lite-tts when maximum fidelity, acting nuance, dialect coverage (130 languages vs 101), complex multi-speaker dialogue, heavy vocal-burst tags, difficult pronunciation or long-form stability matter; Flash-Lite is the recommended replacement for gemini-3.1-flash-tts-preview. Both share the same API schema and prompting structure. Overlapping speech/backchannels (listener reactions wrapped in pipe characters inside a speaker turn) work best on gemini-3.8-flash-tts.

Do not send thinking settings for gemini-3.8-live: omit thinking_level and thinking_config from session setup (thinking_level is not supported; the model uses built-in interleaved reasoning with a fixed latency profile). For configurable reasoning use gemini-3.8-live-extended-thinking instead.
Request AUDIO as the only response modality for gemini-3.8-live; if you need text, enable output_audio_transcription in the setup config instead of asking for text output.

Do not set proactive_audio: false (or configure proactivity) on gemini-3.8-live: proactive audio is permanently enabled and disabling it returns an error. Remove enable_affective_dialog settings as well, since affective dialogue was removed.

Function calling on gemini-3.8-live supports both synchronous (BLOCKING) and asynchronous (NON_BLOCKING) behavior; set the behavior on the function declaration explicitly, and use SILENT, WHEN_IDLE, or INTERRUPT scheduling in the FunctionResponse for non-blocking tools. The client must handle tool responses manually.

On gemini-3.8-live, send_client_content works throughout the whole session with explicit user or model roles, and sending turn_complete=true unconditionally interrupts active generation. To seed prior history before streaming, set initial_history_in_client_content to true in history_config, and prefer a single summary message for long contexts.

gemini-3.8-live defaults turn coverage to TURN_INCLUDES_AUDIO_ACTIVITY_AND_ALL_VIDEO, so all video frames are sent to the model by default; send video frames only when needed to manage context and cost.

gemini-3.8-live does not support caching, code execution, file search, structured outputs, URL context, Google Maps grounding, image generation, or the Batch API; supported features are Live API, function calling, Search grounding, audio generation, and interleaved reasoning. Limits are 131,072 input and 65,536 output tokens; inputs are text, image, audio, and video-type frames per the page, outputs text and audio.

Use gemini-3.8-live as the default for low-latency conversational voice agents where immediate turn-taking matters and reasoning delays are unwanted (fast tools such as reading sensor values); choose gemini-3.8-live-extended-thinking when higher background reasoning is needed. Migrating from gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview means changing the model string and applying the removals above.

Live API prompting: give each agent its own system instruction with name, role and persona; specify the output language whenever you specify an accent; tell the model the conditions under which each tool should be called (names, descriptions, parameters, invocation conditions); state tool calls in distinct sentences; and include examples of what the model should and should not do. Live API expects user input before responding, so include a prompt that asks it to greet the user to start the conversation.

Live API audio streaming: send small audio chunks (20ms-40ms recommended, up to 100ms), do not buffer input audio significantly, resample microphone input to 16kHz, discard the client audio buffer immediately on an interrupted server_content message, and use ContextWindowCompressionConfig for long sessions because native audio tokens accumulate quickly (without compression audio-only sessions are limited to 15 minutes, audio-video to 2 minutes).
Set thinking_config in the session setup with thinking_level of low, medium, or high; MINIMAL is not supported on gemini-3.8-live-extended-thinking.

Declare every function with behavior NON_BLOCKING; only asynchronous function calling is supported, and synchronous blocking calls return an error. The SILENT, WHEN_IDLE and INTERRUPTED scheduling options are not supported on this model.

turnComplete: true no longer means the model is idle. Keep listening for tool calls and audio frames after it arrives, and read interaction_status on BidiGenerateContentServerContent (IN_PROGRESS means processing, background reasoning or awaiting async tool responses; IDLE means all work is done) before closing the session.
Proactive audio is always on for this model; setting proactive_audio to false returns an error. Remove any enable_affective_dialog settings because affective dialogue was removed from the API.
send_client_content works throughout the session (seeding history and mid-turn updates) with explicit user or model roles; setting turn_complete=true immediately interrupts active generation.

Model limits and capabilities: 131,072 input tokens and 65,536 output tokens; supports Live API, thinking, search grounding, audio generation and async function calling; does not support Batch API, caching, code execution, file search, Google Maps grounding, image generation, structured outputs or URL context.

Choose gemini-3.8-live-extended-thinking when background reasoning is needed (multi-step diagnostics, coordinated data retrieval, STEM and code tutoring, masking long tool latency); for low-latency conversational voice without reasoning delays use gemini-3.8-live, which does not take thinking_level.

The model can speak intermediate conversational fillers while it reasons or tools run; turnComplete ends an utterance while interaction_status governs session lifecycle, so return the client to idle only when status is IDLE.

Async function calling is required on gemini-3.8-live-extended-thinking; the Live API does not handle tool responses automatically, so the client must send FunctionResponse objects (with call id, name, response) via send_tool_response.

Set the task_type field in the embedContent method to optimize gemini-embedding-001 embeddings for the intended use. Supported values are SEMANTIC_SIMILARITY, CLASSIFICATION, CLUSTERING, RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT, RETRIEVAL_QUERY, CODE_RETRIEVAL_QUERY, QUESTION_ANSWERING and FACT_VERIFICATION.

For retrieval with gemini-embedding-001, embed queries with RETRIEVAL_QUERY and the documents to be retrieved with RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT. CODE_RETRIEVAL_QUERY, QUESTION_ANSWERING and FACT_VERIFICATION query-side types are likewise paired with RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT for the corpus side.

gemini-embedding-001 outputs 3072-dimensional vectors by default. Use the output_dimensionality parameter to shrink them. Supported range is 128 to 3072, and the recommended sizes are 768, 1536 and 3072.
With gemini-embedding-001, any embedding whose dimensionality is not 3072 must be normalized manually (divided by the vector norm), and the resulting norm should be very close to 1.
gemini-embedding-001 accepts text input only, with an input token limit of 2,048 tokens per input, so longer text must be truncated or chunked before embedding.
When latency is not a concern, use the Gemini Embeddings models with the Batch API, which gives much higher throughput at 50% of the default Embedding price.

Migration: the embedding spaces of gemini-embedding-001 and gemini-embedding-2 are incompatible, so moving to gemini-embedding-2 requires re-embedding all existing data. gemini-embedding-2 does not support task_type (it uses prompt-prefix formatting), whereas gemini-embedding-001 uses the task_type parameter and needs manual normalization for non-3072 dimensions.
Compare embedding vectors with cosine similarity, which focuses on direction rather than magnitude (range -1 to 1).
Keep each embedding request within the model's 8,192-token input limit.
Set output dimensionality anywhere from 128 to 3072; the page recommends 768, 1536 or 3072.
Supply input only as text, image, video, audio or PDF; the page lists these as the supported input modalities and lists the output as text embeddings (vectors), not generated content.

The model page does not cover task types, prompt formatting, normalization or migration. It points to the Embeddings page, which documents gemini-embedding-2 (not the -preview id), so guidance from that page should not be assumed to apply to the preview model.

Set thinking effort with the thinking_level field (generation_config: {thinking_level: "..."}); gemini-nano-banana-2.1 supports minimal, medium and high, with medium as the default (the 3.1 Flash Image models only offer minimal and high, default minimal).
Thinking is enabled by default for Gemini 3 image models and cannot be disabled in the API, so choose a thinking_level rather than trying to turn thinking off.

Request image output via response_format with type image, plus optional mime_type, aspect_ratio and image_size; image_size must use an uppercase K (1K, 2K, 4K), because lowercase such as 1k is rejected. gemini-nano-banana-2.1 supports 1K, 2K and 4K but not 512px, and the default is 1K.
By default gemini-nano-banana-2.1 returns both text and an image unless response_format is set to image only; default output size matches the input image, or is 1:1 if there is no input image.
gemini-nano-banana-2.1 adds extreme aspect ratios 1:4, 4:1, 1:8 and 8:1 (14 ratios total from 1:1 to 21:9, each at 1K, 2K and 4K), at 1,120 / 1,680 / 2,520 output image tokens for 1K / 2K / 4K.

For multi-image input, gemini-nano-banana-2.1 supports up to 14 reference images total, with character resemblance for up to 4 characters and fidelity for up to 10 objects in one workflow; refer to each input image by position (for example 'the first image') in the prompt.

For iterative editing with gemini-nano-banana-2.1, chain turns by passing previous_interaction_id set to the prior interaction.id; the page calls multi-turn the recommended way to iterate on images. Use explicit preservation wording such as 'Keep everything else in the image exactly the same' for inpainting-style edits.

Enable Search grounding on gemini-nano-banana-2.1 with tools=[{type: google_search}]; add search_types [web_search, image_search] for Image Search (only on 2.1 and 3.1 Flash Image). When Image Search is used, the search_suggestions from the google_search_result step must be displayed, and real-world images of people from web search are not supported.
gemini-nano-banana-2.1 accepts video input (public YouTube URL in uri, or a Files API upload) in addition to text, image and PDF; audio input is not accepted for image generation.

gemini-nano-banana-2.1 does not support caching, function calling, structured outputs, code execution, URL context, file search, Live API, Flex or Priority inference, or Maps grounding; it supports Batch API, image generation, Search grounding and thinking. Input limit 131,072 tokens, output limit 32,768.

Parse interleaved responses by iterating interaction.steps where step.type is model_output and checking each content block type for text or image; the convenience properties output_image and output_text only return the last image or the text and miss parts. Thought summaries are read from steps of type thought.

Image prompting best practices: be specific about materials and shapes, state the image purpose, iterate one change at a time, build complex scenes in steps, describe what you want rather than what you do not want, and use camera language (wide-angle, macro). For text in images, specify exact text, font style and design; results are better if you generate the text first and then ask for an image containing it.

Call gemini-omni-1.1-flash through the Interactions API (a POST to the v1beta interactions endpoint on generativelanguage.googleapis.com, or client.interactions.create in the SDKs) with model set to gemini-omni-1.1-flash; the stable model code is gemini-omni-1.1-flash and the preview id gemini-omni-flash-preview is shut down, so migrate to the stable id.
The model accepts text, image and video input (video input up to 10s for editing and extension) and outputs video only (3s-10s at 360p/720p/1080p/4K, 24 FPS), with a 1,048,576-token context window.
Control output with response_format: aspect_ratio is 9:16 or 16:9 (16:9 is the default) and resolution is 360p, 720p (default), 1080p (upscaled) or 4k (upscaled).

Do not rely on system instructions, temperature, top_p, stop sequences or negative-prompt parameters, which this model does not support; express negatives in the prompt text (for example 'No dialogue', 'No extra sound effects', 'Do not do X').

Prompt for text-to-video with scene description, camera movement, lighting and mood, and describe the audio you want (for example 'Include calm background music'); the model generates a default audio track but music needs explicit description. To avoid multiple shots, ask for 'a single continuous shot' or 'No scene cuts'.

For image-to-video, use high-resolution reference images and give specific motion, camera and environmental-effect descriptions (vague prompts such as 'make it move' give weaker results); for first/last-frame interpolation pass two images in input (first, then last) and describe the transition in text.

Try natural-language prompting first and set generation_config.video_config.task (text_to_video, image_to_video, reference_to_video, edit, extend) only as a fallback, because task adds strict constraints; do not put control strings such as FIRST_FRAME or IMAGE_REF_0 written inside angle brackets in prompts, describe each media input's role in words instead.

For multi-turn editing, chain turns with previous_interaction_id (each turn yields a new video), keep edit prompts simple and minimal, and add 'Keep everything else the same' for targeted edits; store=false makes the generated video non-editable in later turns.

For faster synchronous generation set background=false, store=false and stream=false; for outputs larger than 4MB set response_format.delivery to 'uri' and download via the Files API (poll until ACTIVE), since the default returns inline base64 video data.

Stated limitations: no reasoning across multiple videos (degraded performance), video references max 3 clips of up to 3s each with reference audio ignored, no audio reference uploads, no YouTube video sources, no provisioned throughput; English is fully supported while other languages are not evaluated.

Gemini Robotics ER 2 Preview (gemini-robotics-er-2-preview) takes text, image, video and audio input and returns text only, with a 131,072 input token limit and a 65,536 output token limit; the Live API is not supported on this endpoint (use gemini-robotics-er-2-streaming-preview for real-time streaming).

On gemini-robotics-er-2-preview the supported features are caching, code execution, computer use, file search, function calling, Google Maps grounding, Search grounding, structured outputs, thinking and URL context; the Batch API is supported, while flex and priority inference are not.

Migrate from gemini-robotics-er-1.6-preview (shut down) by replacing the model string with gemini-robotics-er-2-preview (standard) or gemini-robotics-er-2-streaming-preview (real-time Live API streaming).

For spatial outputs, ask for JSON and state the schema in the prompt; points are returned as y, x pairs (y first) normalized to 0-1000, and bounding boxes use separate keys label, y, x, y2, x2 also normalized to 0-1000. Cap result counts in the prompt, for example 'Point to no more than 10 items in the image.'

To use agentic vision, enable code execution with tools=[{"type": "code_execution"}] and ask explicitly in the prompt for the behavior wanted, e.g. 'Please Zoom and crop the image for a clearer view', and, if an edited image is needed, 'You must return the final image to the API caller.'
To enforce strict JSON output, state the format in the prompt and add a system_instruction such as 'Be precise. When JSON is requested, reply with ONLY that JSON (no preface, no code block).'

For task orchestration, declare each robot tool with type, name, description and a parameters object whose parameter descriptions carry behavioral guidance; pass the tools list on every interactions.create call including follow-ups; loop by executing each function_call step, returning a function_result with call_id set to the step id and previous_interaction_id set to the prior interaction, and cap iterations (the example uses max_steps = 15).

In orchestration prompts, state the coordinate frame and origin in the user text, ask the model to locate objects and compute coordinates before acting, and leave sequencing to the model with an instruction like 'Call the appropriate sequence of functions to complete this operation.'

Best practices: use plain natural language and try synonyms if a term fails; crop or zoom on small or unclear objects; split complex tasks into one prompt per step; for high-precision tasks query several times and average spatial outputs to reduce variance.
